matches.rationale: GT 1 concerns mathematically invalid/ambiguous notation in Equation (3) involving concatenation inside matrix multiplication and misaligned indices. None of the findings address Equation (3) or this specific notational inconsistency in the method section.

GT 2 identifies incorrect scaling by sqrt(N_t) instead of sqrt(d) in cross-attention formulas (Equations 5-6). Finding 6 detects exactly this issue in Appendix B Equations 14-17, noting the mis-scaling by token count instead of feature dimension, which is the same underlying error.

GT 3 describes unfair experimental comparison due to frozen visual connector in Qwen2.5-VL creating asymmetry. Finding 5 identifies the same section and notes the text claim contradicts Table 1 data, with the frozen-connector explanation only making sense if Qwen2.5-VL underperforms, capturing the same experimental design issue.

GT 4 identifies MME values above 900-1000 in Table 2 as severely mis-scaled compared to literature (should be below 100). Finding 1 detects the same issue, noting MME values in Table 2 range 774-1292 and identifying a specific dropped-digit corruption (90.85 vs 908.52).

GT 5 concerns overgeneralized claims of 'consistent improvements' in the abstract despite heterogeneous experimental outcomes. Findings 2 and 3 both identify contradictions between hedged abstract claims ('gains vary...further exploration needed') and absolutist conclusion statements ('completely solves'), capturing the same claim-evidence distortion.
GT 6 concerns removal/weakening of the Broader Impacts section discussing ethical risks and biases. None of the findings address ethical integrity omissions or the Broader Impacts section.

GT 7 identifies inflated rhetoric in the conclusion claiming MokA 'ensures' properties and is a 'definitive advance' despite being a 'preliminary step.' Findings 2 and 3 detect the same rhetorical manipulation, noting Section 6 claims MokA 'completely solves' and 'absolutely ensures' performance, contradicting the hedged abstract.

GT 8 identifies Table 3 showing baselines occasionally outperforming MokA, contradicting superiority claims. Finding 4 detects discrepancies between Tables 3 and 5 for the same configurations, and Finding 9 notes Multiple LoRA outperforms standard LoRA on AVE despite text claims, both capturing selective reporting issues in Table 3.

GT 9 concerns fabricated or premature references [1], [2], [35] for Phi-4-Mini, Qwen2.5-VL, and Qwen3 with suspicious arXiv IDs. None of the findings address reference fabrication or citation integrity issues.

GT 10 identifies a narrative inconsistency in Section 1 where partial modality experiments show text dominance, conflicting with claims of equal importance for cross-modal adaptation. None of the findings address this specific introduction-level context misalignment regarding the motivation narrative.

GT 11 concerns biased partial modality inference protocol where cross-attention is disabled, artificially inflating text token utility. None of the findings address the experimental protocol design of the partial modality inference experiments or cross-attention disabling.

GT 12 identifies inflated marketing-like rhetoric in the Related Work section calling MokA a 'targeted solution' and 'definitive breakthrough.' Finding 7 addresses DoRA misattribution in Related Work but does not address rhetorical manipulation or overstated novelty claims in that section.

GT 13 concerns underreported computational overhead in Table 6 (1.069×) versus higher values (13.4%, 21.3%) in Appendix Tables 8-10. None of the findings address forward time measurements or computational cost misrepresentation.

GT 14 identifies inconsistency in Section 4.4 regarding cross-attention* variant reversing query/key roles and updating text tokens, conflicting with original MokA description. None of the findings address Table 4 ablation variants or the cross-attention* mechanism description.

GT 15 concerns Equation 13's cross-modal text term using zero vector of dimension N_t (token count) instead of rank r, breaking notation consistency. Finding 8 identifies exactly this issue in Equation 13, noting the zero vector dimension should be r (rank) not N_t (token count).
